images.caption: The Diamantina river in central Australia floods occasionally. Most of the time the Diamantina isn't in flow but remains as disconnected pools like this. In the dry central region of Australia such pools are important water sources. This is a typical sight, showing the impact of the river channel on the vegetation. In particular there is a fringe of Eucalyptus coolibah along the channel edge, and closer to the water there is a "bath ring" of various plants which thrive only at the water's edge. Although some Eucalyptus species are well known for their adaptations to fire, Coolabahs seem to be adapted for flooding, especially in relation to the establishment of seedlings. Once established they can access groundwater, enabling them to persist during drought. >> Processing note >> This is a high dynamic range image generated by merging of 5 different exposures, to enable the full dynamic range of this high-contrast scene to be captured. Tone mapping was also carried out as part of the HDR process, this affects the saturation and colour balance of the image to help bring out certain details.
